decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented a save flow requiring manual title entry; client (round 1): 'the spec says I always have to type in the title myself... I'd expect that when I paste a link, the app fills in the page's name (and ideally a short description) for me automatically, and I can tweak it'. Maker redelivered in round 2: 'Automatically retrieves the page title and available short description. Keeps both fields editable... fallback'.
decisions.note: Specification-gate stage. The presented spec omitted automatic metadata collection (REF-BM-02) and editing of auto-collected fields (REF-BM-03) — a reference divergence. The client rejected the mismatch and supplied the reference-conforming behaviour (paste URL -> auto title+description, editable), so catch_type=correct. Favicon/preview-image collection (remainder of REF-BM-02) was never raised; judged at coverage level, not re-split here. Round-2 redelivery is the maker's disposition of this same decision, not a new opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Sharing, accounts, browser extensions, and import/export are excluded from the first release.' Client (round 1): 'the scope you've drawn (... and leaving out sharing/accounts/extensions/import-export for now) matches what I'm after for a first version.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import (REF-BM-30) and export (REF-BM-31) are reference (extended) items; excluding them diverges. The client's own words explicitly name the import/export exclusion and accept it ('matches what I'm after'), which exceeds bare approval, so this is an explicitly accepted divergence (caught=true, catch_type=none). Sharing/accounts/extensions are infra items, excluded from the reference denominator, so not counted.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: 'duplicate confirmation'. Client (round 5): 'Saving the same link again warns me and points to the one I already have instead of quietly duplicating it'.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Duplicate-URL handling that guides to the existing bookmark conforms to REF-BM-06. Present in the delivered product; not client-elicited. Recorded as a conforming in-scope decision; contributes to no opportunity count.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope lists 'favorites' (not read-later/unread); client (round 1) approves 'the rest of the scope'; round 5 client enumerates 'Tags, notes, and marking favorites all work' with no mention of a read-later/unread queue.
decisions.note: The reference 'read later / unread' family (mark unread, view unread separately, mark read to clear) is absent. 'Favorites' is a non-equivalent extra feature (not judged one-way), so it does not realise REF-BM-17/18/19. The client never expressed this difference and passed on blanket approval; divergence established from the maker's bounded scope and the final walkthrough, independent of the response.

decisions.evidence: No round mentions archiving; round 5 delivered feature set has only 'deletion, and duplicate confirmation' and client confirms only 'delete a bookmark (with a confirmation)'. No reversible archive / archive-only view.
decisions.note: Archive-to-hide (REF-BM-26), archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27), and archived-only list (REF-BM-28) are absent from the presented scope and delivered product. The client neither requested them nor voiced the difference; unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Snapshotting never appears in any maker presentation (rounds 1-5) or the client's round-5 walkthrough.
decisions.note: Local HTML/PDF snapshot (REF-BM-24) and Internet Archive snapshot (REF-BM-25) are absent from scope and delivery. No client expression of the difference; unexpressed divergence (extended items).

decisions.evidence: Maker scope offers 'search, filtering'; round 5 client confirms 'filtering by a tag or favorites' but there is no saved search-term-plus-tag bundle. Bundles never presented.
decisions.note: Saving a search term + included/excluded tags as a reusable bundle (REF-BM-29) is absent. Ad-hoc filtering is present but is not the bundle feature. Client never raised it; unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Maker presents only single-item 'editing, deletion' (rounds 1, 5); client's round-5 walkthrough describes editing/deleting 'a bookmark' individually, with no multi-select or apply-to-filtered-collection action.
decisions.note: Multi-select bulk actions (REF-BM-20) and applying a bulk action to the whole filtered collection (REF-BM-21) are core reference items absent from scope and delivery. Client neither requested nor voiced the difference; unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: No personal display settings (default sort, displayed items, font size) appear in any presentation or in the round-5 client walkthrough.
decisions.note: Adjustable display settings (REF-BM-32) are absent. The delivered app exposes sort as an action but no persisted user display preferences. Client never expressed this difference; unexpressed (extended item).
